newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed on Friday from New York's closing levels ahead of a batch of U.S economic data next week.
Wall Street's 27-point drop on Thursday was also seen as a slightly bearish factor but steady bond markets may see the Dow inch forward at the start of trade later today, dealers said.

"With the yield on the (U.S. 30-year)long bond below seven percent, the market may be more confident today," one dealer said. "But I can't see the Dow doing a lot ahead of the U.S. jobs data next week."
Figures out next week include U.S. personal income and spending figures for April as well as the May report from the National Association of Purchasing Managers.
U.S. leading indicators, factory orders also precede the key unemployment and wage inflation data for May, due on Friday.
McDonalds Corp was down $1/4 to $49-3/4 on continued uncertainties about the fast-food giant's current marketing strategy, which includes discounted sandwiches.
On Friday, the Wall Street Journal reported that the company had backed off an idea to guarantee customers in the U.S. it could deliver their order within 55 seconds of having paid for it.
Auto stocks were generally lower with General Motors Corp down $1/4 to $56-5/8 while Chrysler Corp eased $1/4 to $32-1/8.
The June T-bond was up 4/32 to 109-14/32 while the yield on the benchmark long bond stood at 6.98 percent. The June S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.30 to 845.20.
